names: FR-38 gate at the Middle Fork Nooksack bridge
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mt. Baker Ranger District) — Mount Baker Wilderness above the private timberland
storedPass: No Northwest Forest Pass applies at the private-timberland gate; the landowner's paid recreation permit is what is required here.
No developed fee trailhead here — FR 38 gate/pullout is an undeveloped roadside parking spot; no Northwest Forest Pass required.
drive: From the gated bridge over the Middle Fork Nooksack at the end of FR-38 (~1,200 ft): bike or walk the logging-road network toward Dailey Prairie and the Twin Sisters climbers' paths

names: SR-20 Wine Spires pullout / Burgundy Col climbers' trail
landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest (Methow Valley Ranger District)
storedPass: Not needed at the SR-20 roadside pullout used for the Wine Spires. A Northwest Forest Pass is required at Washington Pass Overlook, Blue Lake, and Cutthroat trailheads — $5/day or $30/annual (America the Beautiful pass also honored).
drive: From Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east past the hairpin turn to the next major pullout, near milepost 166; park there.

names: FR-1570 (Kindy Creek Road) washout parking
landManager: Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest — Glacier Peak Wilderness (Mt. Baker Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass / America the Beautiful Pass
drive: From Cascade River Road mile ~14.2 onto FR-1570 across the Cascade River bridge; park at the boulder-blocked Y-junction (~1,200 ft) and walk the closed roadbed

names: Skyline Lake Trailhead
landManager: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Skykomish Ranger District)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required at developed trailheads.
drive: From the start of US 2 in Everett, drive US 2 east about 65 miles to Stevens Pass, pass under the pedestrian overpass and turn left into the large lot on the north side of the highway.

names: Mt. Baker Ski Area upper lot (Bagley Lakes Trailhead)
drive: From Glacier, drive Mount Baker Highway (SR 542) east to the upper Mt. Baker Ski Area parking lot at the Bagley Lakes Trailhead, milepost 54.6. The highway is gated here for the season and has been closed beyond since October 25, 2026, so this is where cars stop in winter; in summer the road continues to the Artist Point lot.

names: Hidden Lake Trailhead
landManager: National Park Service — North Cascades National Park (Stephen Mather Wilderness)
storedPass: Northwest Forest Pass at the Hidden Lake trailhead.
drive: From Marblemount, drive Cascade River Road (FR-15) about 10.2 paved miles, then turn onto FR-1540 (Sibley Creek Road) and follow its rough gravel surface 4.5 miles to the small Hidden Lake Trailhead (~3,600 ft; Northwest Forest Pass required to park).

names: Forest Road 9020 pullout
drive: From I-90 Exit 38 follow Homestead Valley Road to Forest Road 9020, just before the road goes under the freeway, and drive about 0.2 miles to a pullout on the right at an old abandoned road.

names: US 2 pullouts near milepost 94
drive: Drive US 2 through Tumwater Canyon to any roadside pullout near milepost 94, where the flow can be seen from the road.
